title: Old vines in California
subtitle: Heritage vineyards
objectives: Explain why old Zinfandel vines matter

steps.title: Old vines
steps.body: Some Californian Zinfandel vineyards date from the 1880s, having survived phylloxera and Prohibition. During Prohibition, from 1920 to 1933, Zinfandel was popular with home winemakers, so many vines were kept. Old, head-trained vines give low yields and concentrated, balanced fruit. Lodi and Sonoma have many.

steps.title: Field blends
steps.body: Many old Zinfandel vineyards are field blends: Zinfandel interplanted with Petite Sirah, Carignan, Alicante Bouschet, Mourvèdre and others. Grapes are picked and fermented together. Petite Sirah adds colour and tannin, Carignan acidity. These mixed vineyards reflect how 19th century immigrants planted.

steps.prompt: Which grapes are often found in old Zinfandel field blends?
steps.explanation: Riesling isn't part of these red field blends.

steps.title: Heritage
steps.body: The Historic Vineyard Society, founded in 2011, records Californian vineyards planted at least 50 years ago that still produce. It has helped protect old Zinfandel vineyards from being replanted with more profitable grapes. Producers like Ridge, Turley and Bedrock champion them.

steps.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
steps.explanation: California's old vines are a living archive.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Many Californian Zinfandel vines date from the 1880s
Old vineyards are often field blends with Petite Sirah and Carignan
The Historic Vineyard Society protects them
